**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** A `feat`, so per the repo's flow it merges at the next minor cut, not between cuts.

## What looks good

- Clean design: four optional PARAMs, each written only when stated, so legacy `.cl` streams and user scripts read exactly as before — and the conformance goldens prove it.
- Comment forms are genuinely per-dialect (parenthesised, `;` unnumbered, Heidenhain's numbered block), each built on a pattern the script already uses, and the work-offset word comes from the stream's own `WorkOffset` PARAM — no second WCS derivation.
- The user-text cleaning is the right defence for a CAM program: `( ) % ;` (and `*` on Heidenhain) neutralised, printable-ASCII only, 40-char cap applied to each user text, not the line, so `SETUP:`/`OPERATION:` survive. `user_text_never_breaks_a_comment` pins it per dialect.
- Setup name resolves through `setup::effective` (the same law `wcs_slot` reads), so the comment can't disagree with the posted G54 word.
- Excellent test and doc work: four new pinning tests, the Heidenhain form checker taught comment blocks, and `docs/decisions/257-gcode-comments.md` records the dropped options and the hardware fallback.

## Local results (trial-merged with current main `c442118`, merge applied cleanly)

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run` | builds |
| post: `post_engine`, `comp`, lib | 33 + 9 + 0 passed |
| app lib unittests | 92 passed |
| app: `program_comments` (new) | 4 passed |
| app: `heidenhain_block_form` / `fanuc_post` / `regression_models` | 4 / 8 / 2 passed |
| app: `conformance` | 6 passed (78 legacy `.cl` goldens byte-identical) |
| app: `arc_planes` / `control_comp` / `wear_comp` / `lathe_post` / `tormach_post` | 8 / 5 / 5 / 7 / 10 passed |
| app: `probe_op` | 10 passed, 1 failed — pre-existing on main (below) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

Independently of the suite runs I re-checked the two regenerated Heidenhain goldens (`synth_heidenhain.nc`, `heidenhain/arc_planes.nc`) by stripping comment lines and normalising block numbers: motion-identical to main's, confirming the renumbering claim. Your Tormach Hub run plus this closes the machine-side question for that dialect.

The `probe_op` failure is not yours: `every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag` asserts `PROJECT_VERSION == 51` while main is at 53 (the #340/#352 rungs merged after your last sync); neither the test nor the constant is touched here, and it fails on plain main too.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- Heidenhain's `N.. ; text*` form is the one output still untried on hardware. A control that dislikes it alarms (a visible refusal, never silent motion), and the fallback is written down, so this is a release-notes caution rather than a blocker — worth a line in the cut's notes.
- `docs/decisions/257-gcode-comments.md` says Tormach had two identical `onParameter` definitions and both got the hook; in the merged tree there is one definition with the hook (main must have collapsed it). Behaviour is correct, just a doc/branch-state mismatch.
- `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` grew 491 → 518 lines; the 400-line law flags growth in files already over, non-blocking here, but a good split seam (`comment_params` + the PARAM block) for a future refactor.
- The comments ride on by default with no off-switch yet — as you noted, #258 / PR #302 own the property, and one `if` in each `note()` is the documented toggle path.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
